To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PTH stimulates 1,25(OH)2D3 formation and inhibits 24,25(OH)(2)D3 formation in vitro in kidney homogenates of Japanese quail.
the pharmacological actions of PTH on renal vitamin D metabolism in Japanese quail are slower in onset, more prolonged and more sensitive than those of estradiols.
parathyroid hormone (PTH) increases plasma 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D [1,25-(OHI)D] levels and decreases plasma 24,25-dihydrosyvitamin D [24,25-(OI)D] levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of parathyroids on the metabolism of vitamin D in the Japanese quail.
the acute effects of PTH and 17 beta-estradiol on the vitamin D hydroxylation system.
the effects of estradiol on the renal vitamin hydroxylases of Japanese quail.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PTH is a potent stimulator of 1,25-D3 and an inhibitor of 24,25-D3 in Japanese quail, and that the effects of PTH are more pronounced in vitro than in vivo.
PTH stimulates the 1,25(OH)2D3 hydroxylase in the Japanese quail kidney, but the mechanism of action and the physiological importance of this effect are not known.
parathyroid hormone is a potent stimulator of renal 25-(OH)-D3-1α-hydroxylase activity in the Japanese quail.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the acute effects of PTH and estradiol on the renal vitamin-D-hydroxylases are similar in terms of the dose-response relationship, the time-response relationship, the effect of the hormone on the two vitamin D metabolites and the time required for the effects of the hormones to return to normal.
the acute effects of PTH are not as potent as those of estradiols, but are more prolonged.
the effects of estradiol on the vitamin D hydroxlases is more rapid and longer lasting than those of PTH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PTH is a potent stimulator of 1,25(OH)2D3 synthesis, but the response is not as rapid as the one observed with estrogen.
estradiol is a more potent and longer-acting modulator of vitamin D metabolism in quail than PTH.
the effects of parathyroids on vitamin D are dose-dependent, and that the effects on vitamin D are also dependent on the time after administration.
